You write cross-sectional factors for Binance USDT perpetual futures, using daily bars.

A factor is one expression that gives every coin a number each day. A higher number means the coin is expected to do better over the following days. You will be given a one-sentence idea; turn it into a factor.

Data, one value per coin per day:
- Factor('open'), Factor('high'), Factor('low'), Factor('close'): prices
- Factor('volume'): amount traded, in units of the coin
- Factor('quote_volume'): amount traded, in USDT
- Factor('num_trades'): number of trades
- Factor('taker_base_vol'), Factor('taker_quote_vol'): the part of volume and of quote_volume that came from aggressive buyers

Operators:
- Arithmetic and comparisons: + - * / ** > >= < <= == != (a comparison gives 1 or 0)
- Each value on its own: .Abs() .ln() .sign() .pow(x) .clip(lower=a, upper=b) .max(other) .min(other) .fillna(other) .safe_div(other), and where(condition, a, b)
- One coin over its past n days, n a positive integer: .ts_mean(window=n, min_periods=m) .ts_std .ts_var .ts_sum .ts_max .ts_min .ts_median .ts_skew .ts_kurt .ts_rank .ts_zscore .ts_argmax .ts_argmin .ts_decay_linear .ts_product (all take window and min_periods), .ts_quantile(window=n, q=x), .ts_corr(other, window=n), .ts_cov(other, window=n)
- Exponential averages: .EMA(span=n, min_periods=m) .ts_ewm_mean(span=n, min_periods=m)
- Earlier values: .lag(periods=n) .diff(periods=n) .pct_change(periods=n)
- All coins on one day: .sec_rank() .zscore() .demean() .sec_pct() .winsorize(limit=x) .scale() .neutralize(other)

Example: Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=5)) - 1 is each coin's return over the past 5 days.

Every operator only reads the past. Windows and periods must be positive, at most 365.

The factor must be driven by the data the idea talks about and must point the way the idea says: if the idea says something is bearish, the factor must go down when that thing goes up. Values must be comparable across coins, so a coin's price unit must not matter.

Before you answer you can try candidates with the test_factor tool. Give it one expression. It tells you whether the expression computes and, on data from July 2022 to December 2024, its rank IC with the next day's return and its incremental IC, which is what remains after removing liquidity, volatility, short-term reversal and momentum. Higher is better, and an incremental IC of 0.01 to 0.03 is already good.

You may call test_factor at most 5 times, one call per turn. Testing many variants on the same history overfits it, so stop once you have something sound. test_factor does not check that the factor matches the idea; that is up to you. Keep the direction the idea says even if the IC comes out negative: the idea may simply be wrong on this history.

Write Factor('close') with single quotes inside the tool call. When you are done, reply without calling a tool and finish with the factor between <factor> and </factor>. A reply with no factor scores 0.

Idea: A sudden burst of volume usually marks a top, so the coin tends to fall afterwards.

The idea is bearish on volume bursts: when a coin's volume spikes relative to its own recent norm, it should underperform afterwards. So I'll build volume relative to its own history (quote_volume, USDT-denominated, so it's cross-coin comparable) and put the minus sign on the outside to express the bearish direction. First test: simple ratio to the 20-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0128 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

Result: rank IC +0.019 with incremental +0.013, but it fades in 2024 (+0.005). The idea says "sudden", which suggests a short-term spike against a longer baseline rather than a single day against a 20-day mean. Next I'll test a 5-day mean divided by a 60-day mean, still negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

Interesting split: the burst-vs-baseline form raises absolute IC (+0.032) but lowers incremental IC (+0.010) and is flat in 2024 — likely because a short/long volume ratio partly overlaps with recent price run-up, i.e. the reversal style already removed. The "how unusual is today's volume for this coin" idea can also be written outlier-robustly as a within-coin time-series rank; I'll test that.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

The time-series rank keeps the idea's meaning but is outlier-robust, and it gives the best result so far: incremental +0.016 (t=5.8), fading to +0.006 in 2024. Single-day volume is noisy, so I'll make one more change — average volume over 3 days before ranking, keeping the same 20-day window — to see if noise was holding it back.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0323
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0167 (t = 6.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0241, 2023 +0.0204, 2024 +0.0091

The 3-day smoothing helped a little on every count: incremental +0.0167 (t=6.3) and the 2024 slice improved from +0.006 to +0.009, so the burst effect is at least not purely a 2022–2023 artifact. The gain over the previous test is small, so further variants would mostly be fitting this sample; I'll stop and hand in the tested smoother version.

What I found: the idea holds in the direction it states — coins whose recent volume is unusually high relative to their own 20-day history do underperform the next day, and this survives removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum. Expressing "unusual volume" as a within-coin time-series rank (rather than a raw short/long volume ratio) was clearly better on the incremental measure, presumably because a raw burst ratio leans on recent price run-up. The effect is strongest in 2022H2 and weakest in 2024, so it may be decaying; the direction is kept as the idea says and the magnitude is modest.

Idea: A sudden burst of volume usually marks a top, so the coin tends to fall afterwards.

The idea says a sudden volume burst is bearish. The cleanest reading: how big is today's volume relative to the coin's own recent volume — that is cross-coin comparable (a ratio, no price units) and captures "sudden" rather than "big in absolute terms". Then multiply the outer layer by -1 because a burst should predict a fall.

First test: today's `quote_volume` over its own 20-day mean (min_periods 16 = 80% of 20), negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0128 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

Read: the direction is confirmed — the negated volume ratio has rank IC +0.0193 and incremental IC +0.0128 (t=4.6), but it fades from +0.025 in 2022H2 to +0.005 in 2024. One weakness: the 20-day mean includes today's spike in its own denominator, which damps the signal. Next I swap the mean for a 15-day median (min_periods 12), which a single spike cannot inflate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0271
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0152 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0321, 2023 +0.0162, 2024 +0.0056

Read: swapping the mean for the median clearly helped — rank IC 0.0193 → 0.0271, incremental 0.0128 → 0.0152, better in every sub-period. Now the remaining issue is that a raw ratio is very heavy-tailed (one spike can give 20x). Next I replace the ratio with today's volume's percentile inside its own last 20 days (`ts_rank`), which is bounded to 0–1 and still says "how unusual is today's volume", negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Read: the bounded percentile version is a small step up (rank IC 0.0294, incremental 0.0160, and 2023 improves to 0.0196), so it is both simpler and at least as good. The 2024 fade is consistent across every variant, so it looks like a weakening effect rather than a coding problem. One question left: "sudden" may be a shorter-horizon thing than 20 days. Last test — same formula with a 10-day window (min_periods 8).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

Read: halving the window hurt everything (rank IC 0.0197, incremental 0.0099, 2024 down to zero), so 20 days is the right horizon for "unusual volume" here — a burst has to be measured against a long enough baseline. No further hypothesis worth spending a test on, so I stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history and points the way it says — coins whose volume spikes relative to their own recent norm do underperform. Measuring the burst as a bounded within-coin percentile over 20 days, negated, gave rank IC +0.029 and incremental IC +0.016 (t=5.8), better than a mean-based ratio (+0.019/+0.013) and better than a 10-day window. The effect fades over time (+0.030 in 2022H2, +0.020 in 2023, +0.006 in 2024), so it looks like a weakening signal rather than a stable one, and I keep the bearish direction as the idea states it.

Idea: A sudden burst of volume usually marks a top, so the coin tends to fall afterwards.

The idea says a sudden volume burst is bearish, so I need volume measured against the coin's own recent norm (not its absolute level, which isn't comparable across coins) and then flipped in sign. First test: log of quote_volume over its 20-day mean, with the minus sign on the outside.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0128 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

The sign flip gives a positive IC (+0.019) that survives style removal (+0.013, t=4.6) and is positive in all three periods, though it weakens in 2024. The idea stresses *sudden*, so one change: shorten the baseline mean from 20 days to 5 so the factor reacts to a burst rather than a slow drift.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0011
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0008 (t = -0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0076, 2023 -0.0006, 2024 -0.0052

The 5-day baseline collapses to zero (+0.001), so this isn't a one-day spike effect — the 5-day version is mostly short-term reversal, which the incremental IC already strips out. Since longer was better, I'll test the other direction: a 60-day baseline (min_periods 48) against the 20-day version.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0315
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0102 (t = 3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0170, 2023 +0.0178, 2024 -0.0008

The 60-day baseline raises absolute IC (0.0315) but *lowers* incremental IC (0.0102) and goes negative in 2024 — the classic sign of loading on a known liquidity/size style rather than the idea. So 20 days stays the best. One more single change on that form: volume is heavy-tailed, so the mean baseline gets inflated by past spikes; a 20-day *median* baseline (min_periods 16) is a more robust way to say "bigger than usual".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0314
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0177 (t = 6.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0292, 2023 +0.0216, 2024 +0.0079

The median baseline improves on every measure at once: rank IC 0.0314 vs 0.0193, incremental IC 0.0177 (t=6.3) vs 0.0128, and it is positive in all three periods (2022H2 +0.029, 2023 +0.022, 2024 +0.008). That is a clear improvement, so I stop here rather than spend the last test on further tuning of the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, in the direction it states — a coin trading well above its own typical USDT turnover over the past month tends to underperform the next days. The "sudden" part matters less than the manual reading suggests: a 5-day baseline gives nothing (+0.001, i.e. it is just short-term reversal), a 60-day baseline loads on liquidity/size style (high absolute IC, lower incremental, negative in 2024), and a robust 20-day *median* baseline is best on every measure. Note it decays over time (0.029 → 0.022 → 0.008), so the effect is weaker in 2024, but it never flips sign, which is what I want to keep.

Idea: A coin trading near its recent high is strong and keeps rising.

The idea is "a coin trading near its recent high is strong and keeps rising": the key quantity is the gap between the close and its recent high, and the direction is positive — the closer to the high, the more bullish. To make it comparable across coins I use a ratio rather than a price difference: close divided by the highest high of the last 20 days, which is 1 at a fresh high and falls off as the coin drops away from it. Window 20 with min_periods 16 follows the 80% rule.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0027
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0010 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 +0.0005, 2024 +0.0019

The ratio came out almost flat: rank IC +0.0027 and incremental IC +0.001, so within 20 days a coin sitting near its high carries essentially no information here — the 20-day high is close to a short-term momentum/reversal signal, which is already stripped out. The one thing I'll change is the horizon: a 60-day high is a slower "trend vs. drawdown" measure rather than a short-term one, and it still expresses exactly the idea. min_periods 48 is 80% of 60.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0058
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0045 (t = 1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0053, 2023 +0.0048, 2024 +0.0038

The 60-day version is interesting: raw rank IC turns slightly negative (-0.0058) but incremental IC is +0.0045 and, importantly, positive in all three periods (2022H2, 2023, 2024), so the signal survives style removal in a stable way. It is still weak, though. Now I keep the 60-day horizon and change only the normalization: instead of the ratio to the high, I place the close inside the 60-day high-low range, which also accounts for how deep the trough was. This still says "higher = nearer the recent high", just measured against the range the coin actually covered.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0325
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0013 (t = -0.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0008, 2023 -0.0024, 2024 -0.0003

The range version is clearly worse — incremental IC -0.0013, negative in every period — so normalizing by the depth of the trough destroys the signal; what matters is distance from the high alone. I go back to the 60-day ratio and change one thing: smooth it with a 10-day mean (min_periods 8), because "trading near its high" is a state that persists, and a single day's close is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0065 (t = 2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0067, 2023 +0.0064, 2024 +0.0064

Smoothing clearly helped: incremental IC rises from +0.0045 to +0.0065 (t = 2.2) and, unusually, is nearly identical in all three periods (0.0067 / 0.0064 / 0.0064), while the raw rank IC also turns positive (+0.0045). Since the last accepted step already improved things and further moves would only be window or smoothing tuning on the same history, I stop here rather than spend the fifth test on overfitting.

What I found: measuring "near its recent high" over 20 days carries no information on this history (incremental IC +0.001), and normalizing by the depth of the 60-day range actually breaks it (incremental IC -0.001, negative in every period). Only the plain distance to the 60-day high works, and only after smoothing it over 10 days: the incremental IC is small (+0.0065) but positive in each of the three periods, which is the reassuring part, while the raw IC of +0.0045 says the idea is only mildly true here and not a strong standalone edge. The direction is kept as the idea states — the closer the close is to the recent high, the higher the factor.
